notes: Reviewed unchanged: no unit was altered. Every s### and t### id is partitioned exactly once; 22 source and 31 target tokens accounted for, and every unit is aligned with both heads members of their arrays.

s015 δέ takes both t016 and and t017 yet: s011 καί has already taken t014, no other source token can license either word, and rule 2 offers no smaller defensible split. The head choice between and and yet is the one materially contested point in the verse and is recorded in the unit note; rule 17's refusal of a token chosen merely for standing first is what settles it on yet.

s017 τά follows rule 49's adjective clause — the supplied nominal things is the article's own, since ἐπιτήδεια cannot carry the determiner — rather than being left unrepresented under rule 23. Rule 22 then keeps the head on things and not on the. This is the τὸ τρίτον → the third part shape.
s013 μή is an ordinary negative aligned to not; rules 41, 59 and 79 are not in play, there being no negative indefinite in the clause and no verb of denial.

s004 and s016 are the same dative pronoun analysed two ways because the ASV writes unto for the first and a bare object for the second; the case preposition rides with the pronoun under rules 21 and 36 rather than being split off or left unrepresented.

s022's supplied doth it goes to the predicate noun rather than to τί: rule 68 gives a supplied subject and verb to the predicate where the clause expresses no subject of its own, and rule 96 keeps them there. A reading that gave doth it to the interrogative would have to read the supplied verb off English word order, which rule 63 refuses.
